slides.headline: “Why don’t I feel like it *anymore?*”
slides.lead: The question people are too shy to ask. Swipe.

slides.headline: Usually it’s life, *not a flaw in you.*
slides.body: Stress and exhaustion, poor sleep, hormones, some contraception and medication, and time. Usually several at once.
slides.note: From intimova.ng: Low libido in women, the documented reasons.

slides.headline: For many people it shows up *after closeness begins.*
slides.body: Not as a bolt from the blue. So “I’m never in the mood out of nowhere” isn’t evidence that something’s wrong.

slides.headline: Take the pressure off. *Make room for rest.*
slides.body: Real sleep, real rest, and unhurried closeness with no goal. If there’s a partner, talking openly does more than any product.

slides.headline: Sudden, persistent, distressing, *or after a new medication?*
slides.body: Then it’s worth a conversation with a doctor. The cause is often straightforward, sometimes as simple as adjusting a prescription.

slides.headline: A quieter season *isn’t a verdict on you.*
slides.lead: Send this to someone who’s wondered. Full answer: link in bio.

captions.instagram:
“Why don’t I feel like it anymore?”

The question people are too shy to ask. Usually the answer is life, not a flaw in you: stress and exhaustion, poor sleep, hormones, some contraception and medication, and time. Usually several at once.

And desire doesn’t always come first. For many people it shows up after closeness begins, not before.

What tends to help: take the pressure off, rest properly, and talk. If it’s sudden, persistent, distressing or started with a new medication, see a doctor.

A quieter season isn’t a verdict on you.

Full answer: link in bio.
